scenes.vo: Before the dashboard worked, I had to unlearn three things. Day one — I thought GitHub data was noise. Pull requests, commits, issues — too granular to mean anything at the company level. I was wrong. A single derived metric — fourteen-day commit-velocity acceleration with a contributor-spike confirmation — filters the noise and leaves a signal you can act on. Day two — I trusted my network to show me the deals. My network was showing me yesterday's deals. By the time a partner forwards you a deck, three other funds already have it. The merge graph, watched weekly, shows you tomorrow's deals. Day three — I worried public data had no edge. It does. The data is public. The rhythm — Sunday-morning attention applied every week on a stable methodology — is the moat. Make sense so far?

scenes.vo: Here is what we actually proved. Two hundred nineteen venture-backed startups, across nineteen sectors and five quarterly periods. Companies that registered a two-times contributor spike inside a fourteen-day window preceded their fundraise announcements by a median of thirty-one days, with an interquartile range of twenty-one to forty-seven days. Precision at the thirty-day window — sixty-two percent. The false positives are mostly silent rounds that did not get press, not nothing-happened. Every number I just said is re-derivable from public GitHub data. The regression code is on Zenodo. The full preprint is on SSRN. CC-BY-4-point-zero. You can replicate the panel in an afternoon. Still with me?

faqs.q: Why is this called a VSL when it's also a written page?
faqs.a: The video is the primary asset — a 10-minute Brunson-format VSL with synthetic voice cadence (Cartesia Theo, no founder face or voice). The page below the video is the structured transcript so the same content is consumable in 12 minutes by an investor who would rather skim than watch. Same arc — hook, big domino, three secrets, proof, stack, closes, encore — both formats.
Yes — Cartesia 'Theo'. Anonymity rule: no founder face, voice, or name. Synthetic TTS keeps the methodology in front and the personality out of the way.

faqs.q: What's the proof for the 21–47 day lead band?
faqs.a: An SSRN-published longitudinal panel of 219 venture-backed startups across 19 sectors and 5 quarterly periods. Median pre-deck lead time of 31 days, IQR 21–47. Precision at the 30-day window: 62%. The full panel and regression code are on Zenodo (CC-BY-4.0). Replicate it in an afternoon.

Two reasons. One — there is no sales team, no enterprise motion, no demo gating. The whole price difference is the cost of the sales motion we removed. Two — the buyer is a developer-investor writing €5k–€50k checks, not a partner at a fund with a six-figure data budget. Pricing matches the buyer.

38% false-positive rate at the 30-day window. Of those, ~70% are silent rounds that didn't get press — not no-events. The remaining ~30% are genuine head-fakes (early hiring spikes that didn't translate to a round). The Day 21 follow-up email walks through how we handle them.
